newsitem.title: USA: TWA protests American-British Air alliance.
newsitem.headline: TWA protests American-British Air alliance.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said Thursday it believes the recommendations of a British government agency on the proposed alliance between AMR Corp's American Airlines and British Airways Plc are not enough to protect competition.

In a statement, TWA said the recommendations made by the UK's Office of Fair Trading "fall far short of what is needed to protect the public and would still let the merged airlines crush competitors trying to serve the United States-United Kingdom market."

Earlier, Britain said that it is to resume "open skies" trade talks next month aimed at opening up the trans-Atlantic airline market to free competition. Talks are linked to the proposed alliance between British Airways and American.

TWA said that the conditions proposed by the Office of Fair Trading -- including a liberalized bilateral agreement and transferring a limited number of slots at London's Heathrow Airport -- would not address these market concerns.

TWA said it believes the Office of Fair Trading recommendations overstate the possible benefits of the proposed alliance, but fail to recognize that the American Airlines-British Airways merger would lead to higher fares.
